title: Telemetry Privacy Bridge: incremental scrub, JIT reveal and immutable access ledger for traces
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a 'Telemetry Privacy Bridge' pipeline that sits between trace/log producers and long-term observability storage. The Bridge will perform incremental, policy-driven scrubbing, tag events with provenance metadata, enable just-in-time (JIT) reveal for authorized investigators, and write an immutable access ledger for every reveal. This ticket covers the design and implementation of trace hooks, the scrub/adaptation stage, the JIT reveal broker, and integration with RBAC and KMS for auditing.
background: We currently have multiple incidents where sensitive customer identifiers are observed in trace payloads and retained longer than necessary. Existing scrubbing is batch-based and coarse-grained, causing either over-redaction (hurting debugging) or under-redaction (PII leakage). The Privacy Bridge aims to be stream-native, deterministic in scrubbing decisions, and provide forensicable reveals with strict access logging and TTL re-scrubbing after review completion.
acceptance_criteria: Bridge can attach to existing trace hooks (OtTel/Jaeger) with <5ms additional p95 latency for normal spans
Field-level scrub policies configurable per-tenant and per-route via Console with versioning
Provenance metadata persisted on 100% of transformed spans (policy id, scrub version, operator)
JIT reveal flow decrypts and returns original field values only to users with role-based approval; each reveal emits an immutable ledger entry (sha256) with timestamp and operator id
Retention enforcement automatically prunes re-creatable raw fields after configured TTL unless a valid hold is active
E2E test coverage: unit tests for scrub rules, integration test for reveal flow, and a perf benchmark demonstrating target throughput of 10k spans/s on a single Bridge replica
design_notes: Stream-first architecture: ingest -> deterministic classifier -> redact/transform -> emit transformed span + provenance to fast store -> append raw encrypted payload to escrow with TTL
Policy model: layered policies (global -> org -> route) with explicit allow/deny precedence and policy versioning for rollbacks
Provenance metadata schema: policy_id, policy_version, scrub_outcome, classifier_confidence, bridge_version (stored as tags on spans)
JIT reveal: ephemeral KMS-wrapped key material per-escrowed-batch; reveal broker enforces RBAC + justifications; reveal window configurable per-tenant
Immutable ledger: append-only ledger implemented as write-once objects in S3 prefix + signed manifest (ledger entries hashed + signed by service key)
Performance tradeoffs: encryption of raw payloads increases CPU; consider SKS (shared key store) vs envelope KMS for throughput optimization
technical_notes: Trace hooks: add minimal middleware in our tracing SDK to emit pre-scrub span snapshot to Bridge; hooks must be idempotent and backpressure-aware
Classifier: lightweight regex + ML-based entropy detector for identifying high-risk fields; default denylist applied first
Scrub transforms: support redaction, tokenization (salted hash), truncation, and replace-with-reference (escrow id)
Escrow storage: AES-256-GCM envelope encryption with KMS-managed DEKs; escrow objects rotated and TTL-driven lifecycle managed by Bridge
Reveal broker API: POST /reveal {escrow_id, fields, justification} -> returns signed temporary token; audit events emitted to ledger stream
RBAC integration: Console-managed roles map to reveal permissions; use existing SSO groups and map to reveal-policy bindings
Observability: Bridge must emit internal metrics (scrub_rate, reveal_requests, reveal_success, escrow_size, scrub_latency_p50/p95) and logs with structured tags
Backfill: one-time backfill job to scan recent 90d traces and apply policy transformations into transformed store; careful DB locking and rate limiting required
